From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## Headline view

The Seller's package is not balanced. Its main effect is to move known, quantifiable risks onto the Buyer. It does this in three ways:

1. **Blanket protections.** General disclosure of the whole data room, a broad buyer-knowledge bar, and limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses that apply to "all Claims".
2. **Weakened fundamental protections.** Title, capacity, tax and IP would sit in the same capped, time-limited regime as general warranties.
3. **Known issues left outside the price and completion mechanics.** These are Riverlark, the bonuses, Ironquay, Bluefen and the incident.

The cover letter also contradicts the Seller's own Disclosure Letter on several points, which is useful leverage. For example, it says Bluefen is "addressed", but DL §2 says no consent has been obtained. It calls the incident "not material", but DL §6 says the investigation is preliminary and its scope unknown.

**Known or quantifiable items at stake (before any Bluefen value impact):**

| Item | Amount (AUD) |
|---|---|
| Riverlark facility | ~3,200,000 |
| DD-005 bonuses | 420,000 + on-costs |
| Ironquay SOW3 balance | 180,000 |
| Sandbar renewals | 330,000 |
| **Total** | **≈ 4,130,000+**, about 17% of price and close to the proposed 4.8m cap |

Bluefen (~30% of FY26 revenue) and the DD-006 incident are on top of this.

---

## A. Structural / risk-allocation issues

### 1. Fundamental (title and capacity) warranties under the general cap and time limit. **Reject.**
- Title is the core of the deal. Capping it at 20% means the Buyer could pay 24m and recover only 4.8m if it does not get good title.
- **Push for:**
  - a cap of 100% of the price
  - a time limit of at least 7 years, or the statutory limitation period
  - no de minimis or basket
  - no qualification by disclosure or buyer knowledge
- "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to accept this.

### 2. "Limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise." **Reject the default.**
- This reverses the usual structure. Any carve-out missed in drafting would fall inside the caps.
- **Flip it.** Limitations should apply only to general Warranty Claims. Expressly exclude:
  - fraud and wilful concealment
  - fundamental warranties
  - the tax indemnity / tax warranties
  - specific indemnities
  - leakage and price adjustment
  - covenant breaches and restraints
  - completion obligations

### 3. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5) applying to "Claims of any nature." **Narrow.**
- Expressly carve out fraud, dishonesty and wilful non-disclosure. Liability for fraud cannot effectively be excluded in any event, so drafting should say so.
- Preserve injunctive relief and specific performance.
- Non-reliance should not affect specific indemnities or claims for misleading or deceptive conduct based on Disclosure Letter statements. Note that under ACL s18, non-reliance clauses are relevant but not conclusive.

### 4. General disclosure of the entire data room and public registers (DL §1.1–1.2). **Reject.**
- With a data room cut-off of 22 Sept 2026, this would qualify every warranty against everything in DD-002 to DD-012 and all public records.
- **Push for:**
  - only specific disclosures that are fair, clear and give enough detail for a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and assess its effect
  - only against the specific warranty identified
  - disclosures never to qualify fundamental warranties, the tax indemnity or specific indemnities
  - a data room index annexed and a USB/archive of the data room delivered
  - no "deemed disclosure" of searches beyond named ASIC/PPSR searches on fixed dates
- DL §1.4 ("no admission that consent… is legally required") is acceptable only if specific indemnities override it.
- The Disclosure Letter is dated 22 Sept and it is now 5 Nov. Require a bring-down. Any disclosures made between signing and completion should give the Buyer termination or indemnity rights, not cure breaches.

### 5. Buyer knowledge bar (cl 8.3). **Reject. This is the most dangerous single clause.**
- It covers advisers' knowledge and anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records. Combined with general disclosure, it would remove most warranty protection. It would also arguably defeat claims on the very issues the Buyer has found (Ironquay, the incident, Bluefen).
- **Preferred:** an express pro-sandbagging clause, so Buyer knowledge does not limit claims.
- **Fallback:** limit the bar to the actual knowledge of named Buyer individuals of matters fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter, and never to specific indemnities.

### 6. Caps, thresholds and time limits (cl 12.1–12.3). **Negotiate.**
- **Cap of 20% (4.8m).** Within market range but low given the known issues. Push for 30–50%, or accept 20% only if W&I insurance sits above it and specific indemnities are separately capped at 100%.
- **Basket of 250,000 (~1.04%) on an excess-only basis.** Push for 0.5% (120,000) on a tipping basis, so the full amount is recoverable once the threshold is met.
- **De minimis of 25,000 (~0.1%).** Push for 10,000, with related claims aggregated.
- **18 months for general warranties.** Acceptable, or push for 24 months to cover two audit cycles.
- **Tax.** Time limit should run to the end of the amendment period for the relevant assessment plus 3–6 months.
- **Title.** 7 years or more.
- **Retention / escrow.** Given the open items, seek a retention of about 1.5–2.5m for 18–24 months, or escrow, to secure the specific indemnities.

### 7. Tax and IP "settled under the general regime." **Reject.**
- **Tax:** a standalone tax indemnity covering pre-completion tax (including tax on the bonuses), at 100% cap, with no basket and no disclosure qualification.
- **IP:** warranties should have an extended survival period and should not be generally disclosed against, given Ironquay (below).

---

## B. Deal-specific issues

### 8. Bluefen change of control (DD-002; cl 3 / 6.3). **High priority.**
- Bluefen is about 3.6m of revenue (~30%). Its consent clause 11.2 has conditions in 11.3.
- DL §2 confirms there is no consent and no evidence the conditions are satisfied. The cover letter's "addressed" is wrong.
- Treating the condition as satisfied on "delivery of written consent" is not enough. A consent with conditions attached (repricing, fees, new terms) would satisfy the Seller's drafting but could harm value.
- **Push for:**
  - a condition precedent of an **unconditional** written consent, or one on terms acceptable to the Buyer acting reasonably, with all 11.3 conditions satisfied, in a form approved by the Buyer
  - the condition to be waivable only by the Buyer
  - the Seller to use best (or all reasonable) endeavours, with the Buyer consulted on all communications
  - any cost of meeting the 11.3 conditions borne by the Seller
  - a long-stop date with a Buyer termination right
  - if the Buyer waives, a price adjustment or specific indemnity for loss of the contract
- **Action:** obtain and review DD-002 clause 11.3 now.

### 9. Riverlark facility (~3.2m; DD-003). **High priority.**
- A release "following Completion" is inconsistent with debt-free pricing and leaves security over Company assets after the Buyer has paid. Completion is also likely to trigger change-of-control clause 8.1.
- **Push for:**
  - the facility treated as Debt and repaid from the purchase price via the funds flow at Completion
  - a payout letter, deed of release, and PPSR (and any other) security discharges as Completion deliverables
  - a Seller covenant to obtain Riverlark's waiver of clause 8.1, or standstill, between signing and completion
  - break costs and fees to count as Debt

### 10. DD-005 completion bonuses (420,000). **High priority: leakage / price.**
- The Company is the employer, so it bears the bonuses and on-costs. Leaving them out of the funds flow means the Buyer pays for them.
  - On-costs to check: NSW payroll tax, PAYG withholding, workers' compensation, and super where the bonus is ordinary time earnings. Confirm SG treatment with tax and employment advisers.
- If continued-employment conditions run after Completion, the Buyer bears the retention risk and cost.
- **Push for:**
  - bonuses and all on-costs treated as Transaction Costs / Debt-like items, deducted from the price and paid through payroll at Completion
  - a specific tax and employment indemnity
  - any post-completion-conditional amounts escrowed and funded by the Seller

### 11. Ironquay IP (DD-004 cl 7.3; DD-010). **High priority.**
- Title to the SOW3 Project Materials does not pass until **every** SOW3 fee is paid in cleared funds.
- 180,000 is recorded as open, payment is not verified, and there is no confirmatory assignment. The Company may not own IP it uses. The risk is title and infringement, not just a 180,000 debt.
- The existing indemnity, limited to the SOW3 payment, is inadequate.
- **Push for:**
  - the outstanding amount paid before or at Completion and treated as Debt
  - Ironquay's executed confirmatory assignment (and a release of claims) as a Completion deliverable
  - verification of the true position against bank records
  - a broadened specific indemnity covering third-party claims, injunctions, re-development or licensing costs, and business interruption
  - the indemnity outside the cap, basket and knowledge bar, with at least 6 years' survival

### 12. DD-006 export / privacy incident (~1,240 records). **High priority.**
- The incident involves personal information (names, emails, roles, activity data) sent to an unintended external recipient. The investigation is preliminary.
- Under the Privacy Act 1988 Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, an entity that suspects an eligible data breach must assess it, generally within 30 days. As of 22 Sept that assessment was incomplete, and we are now well past that point. The Seller's "not expected to be material" is unsupported.
- **Push for:**
  - immediate disclosure of the incident timeline, the assessment outcome, any OAIC or individual notifications, recall/deletion confirmations and access logs
  - a pre-completion covenant to complete the assessment and make any required notifications in consultation with the Buyer
  - specific warranties on the investigation's outcome and on compliance
  - a specific indemnity outside the general limitations covering investigation, notification, remediation, third-party claims and regulatory costs
  - drafting the indemnity with care, since indemnities for civil penalties may be unenforceable on public policy grounds
  - if the scope cannot be confirmed before Completion, a Material Adverse Change or termination trigger

### 13. Sandbar supplier renewals (3 × 110,000; DD-008 / DD-011). **Medium priority.**
- The Seller calls these "ordinary course", but DL §8 says the disclosure does not state whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. The "read together" note suggests related or split commitments.
- **Push for:**
  - copies, timing, and confirmation of whether Sandbar is related to the Seller
  - termination rights
  - any commitment above an agreed threshold, or any related-party renewal, to need Buyer consent under the conduct-of-business covenant
  - non-ordinary-course or related-party amounts treated as leakage or Debt-like items
  - a warranty that all supplier contracts are on arm's-length terms

### 14. Title evidence (DD-012). **Strengthen.**
- A share register alone is not enough, and DL §10 expressly disclaims verification.
- **Push for:**
  - a review of ASIC records, the constitution and share certificates, plus PPSR searches against the Seller over the shares
  - warranties that the shares are fully paid and unencumbered, and that there are no options, convertibles or rights to issue
  - signed transfers, certificates and any releases as Completion deliverables
- See item 1 on the warranty regime.

### 15. Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009). **Lower priority. Verify.**
- **Lease:** make the landlord notification a Completion deliverable, or a post-completion covenant with Seller cooperation.
- **Mossvale:** confirm the definition of "assignment" does not include a deemed assignment on change of control. Obtain a warranty that no third-party consent is needed for the sale other than those listed.

---

## Summary of recommendations (priority order)

1. **Reject the anti-sandbagging clause (8.3) and general disclosure (DL §1).** Use specific, fair disclosure only, with no disclosure against fundamentals, tax or indemnities, and seek pro-sandbagging.
2. **Ring-fence fundamentals, tax and specific indemnities.** Use a 100% cap, extended time limits, and no thresholds. Reverse "limitations apply to all Claims", and carve fraud out of the limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses.
3. **Riverlark.** Repay from the price at Completion, with releases and PPSR discharges as deliverables and a waiver of the clause 8.1 change of control.
4. **Bluefen.** Make an unconditional consent, with clause 11.3 satisfied on Buyer-approved terms, a Buyer-waivable condition precedent. Seller bears the costs. Add a termination right or price protection.
5. **Bonuses.** Treat the 420,000 plus on-costs as a Debt-like deduction in the funds flow, with a tax and employment indemnity.
6. **Ironquay.** Require payment, a confirmatory assignment as a Completion deliverable, and a broad uncapped IP indemnity.
7. **DD-006.** Require full status information now, a covenant to complete the NDB assessment and any notifications, and a specific indemnity. Consider making it a Material Adverse Change trigger.
8. **Thresholds and cap.** Push for a 0.5% tipping basket, 10,000 de minimis, and a 30–50% cap or W&I insurance above 20%. Add a retention or escrow of 1.5–2.5m.
9. **Sandbar, title, lease, Mossvale.** Verify, tighten conduct-of-business and leakage provisions, and add Completion deliverables.
10. **Bring the Disclosure Letter up to date** from 22 Sept. Disclosures between signing and completion should not cure breaches.

**Caveat:** This review is based only on the Seller's summary and Disclosure Letter. I have not seen the full SPA, the DD documents or the funds flow, so the clause references and positions should be checked against the actual drafts. The privacy, tax and employment points (NDB timing, SG and payroll tax on the bonuses) need confirmation from specialists before we finalise the mark-up.

### 13. Sandbar supplier renewals (3 × 110,000; DD-008 / DD-011). **Medium priority.**
- The Seller calls these "ordinary course", but DL §8 says the disclosure does not state whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. The "read together" note suggests related or split commitments.
- **Push for:**
  - copies, timing, and confirmation of whether Sandbar is related to the Seller
  - termination rights
  - any commitment above an agreed threshold, or any related-party renewal, to need Buyer consent under the conduct-of-business covenant
  - non-ordinary-course or related-party amounts treated as leakage or Debt-like items
  - a warranty that all supplier contracts are on arm's-length terms

### 14. Title evidence (DD-012). **Strengthen.**
- A share register alone is not enough, and DL §10 expressly disclaims verification.
- **Push for:**
  - a review of ASIC records, the constitution and share certificates, plus PPSR searches against the Seller over the shares
  - warranties that the shares are fully paid and unencumbered, and that there are no options, convertibles or rights to issue
  - signed transfers, certificates and any releases as Completion deliverables
- See item 1 on the warranty regime.

### 15. Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009). **Lower priority. Verify.**
- **Lease:** make the landlord notification a Completion deliverable, or a post-completion covenant with Seller cooperation.
- **Mossvale:** confirm the definition of "assignment" does not include a deemed assignment on change of control. Obtain a warranty that no third-party consent is needed for the sale other than those listed.

## Summary of recommendations (priority order)

1. **Reject the anti-sandbagging clause (8.3) and general disclosure (DL §1).** Use specific, fair disclosure only, with no disclosure against fundamentals, tax or indemnities, and seek pro-sandbagging.
2. **Ring-fence fundamentals, tax and specific indemnities.** Use a 100% cap, extended time limits, and no thresholds. Reverse "limitations apply to all Claims", and carve fraud out of the limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses.
3. **Riverlark.** Repay from the price at Completion, with releases and PPSR discharges as deliverables and a waiver of the clause 8.1 change of control.
4. **Bluefen.** Make an unconditional consent, with clause 11.3 satisfied on Buyer-approved terms, a Buyer-waivable condition precedent. Seller bears the costs. Add a termination right or price protection.
5. **Bonuses.** Treat the 420,000 plus on-costs as a Debt-like deduction in the funds flow, with a tax and employment indemnity.
6. **Ironquay.** Require payment, a confirmatory assignment as a Completion deliverable, and a broad uncapped IP indemnity.
7. **DD-006.** Require full status information now, a covenant to complete the NDB assessment and any notifications, and a specific indemnity. Consider making it a Material Adverse Change trigger.
8. **Thresholds and cap.** Push for a 0.5% tipping basket, 10,000 de minimis, and a 30–50% cap or W&I insurance above 20%. Add a retention or escrow of 1.5–2.5m.
9. **Sandbar, title, lease, Mossvale.** Verify, tighten conduct-of-business and leakage provisions, and add Completion deliverables.
10. **Bring the Disclosure Letter up to date** from 22 Sept. Disclosures between signing and completion should not cure breaches.
